source_note: 以研究项目准确标注的北洞中心柱西面主尊为主体，以2025年CC0实拍补充底座。保留无双手、残缺袖臂、胸腹与面颊剥蚀和不完整火焰背光；只作稀疏线条概括，不修复缺手、不添加手印。选取主尊与背光局部，不画全山或整窟；相邻胁侍不在构图范围。输入输出均已目视检查。照片现存彩绘与历史补修不作为北齐原彩绘年代判断依据。
prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: a single fine-line architectural illustration for the Chinese heritage collection 访古.
Image 1 is the STYLE MASTER, an existing Vairocana Buddha contour drawing. Match its elegant, delicate, slightly organic thin lines, restrained detail, generous blank areas, and consistent visual density. Image 2 (and subsequent photos if applicable) is SUBJECT GEOMETRY ONLY: draw the actual named monument in that reference, preserving its identifying silhouette, roof type, visible storey count, bay count, openings, and proportions.
Create a refined, sparse BLACK INK ON PURE WHITE line drawing. Use confident fine contours with a few finer internal structural lines. All surfaces remain WHITE; use outlines for doors and windows rather than dark fills. No solid shadows, no broad grey shading, no crosshatching, no pencil grain, no texture, no gradient. No color, no gold, no black background. The white will become transparent and the ink the relevant dynasty color in the website.
Show the complete monument, centered, approximately straight-on at facade level, with verticals vertical and minimal perspective. Use only a few short ground lines. Remove tourists, foliage, vehicles, wires, modern signage, fences obstructing the structure, neighboring distractions and sky. Preserve architectural ornament selectively, without filling every roof tile or brick. No invented features. No labels, letters, calligraphy, dimension lines, captions, watermark, frame or border.
Subject is NOT an exterior building. Draw ONLY the seated CENTRAL BUDDHA on the FRONT/WEST face of the central pillar in NORTHERN XIANGTANGSHAN NORTH CAVE, also called BIG BUDDHA CAVE / DAFO CAVE, modern cave9 北响堂山第9窟大佛洞中心柱正面主尊. Image2 is the university research project's verified FRONTAL photograph of this exact figure and flame aureole. Image3 is a 2025 close oblique photograph of the SAME central figure, showing the actual surviving lotus-base profile and missing parts. Use image2's frontal orientation and the figure's real proportions; use image3 only for base, stone damage and finer head details. The image1 Buddha is STYLE ONLY, do not copy its Tang face or pose. Preserve this Northern Qi Buddha's very broad rounded face, low curled-hair cap and small ushnisha, broad shoulders, solid upright chest, robe covering BOTH shoulders with fine parallel curved folds, thick crossed legs and compact high lotus pedestal. CRITICAL: preserve the ACTUAL MISSING FOREARMS AND HANDS: BOTH hands are absent. Do not invent palms, fingers, a mudra or hands resting in the lap. Keep the cut or broken sleeve/arm edges at their real photographed positions and the wide worn patches interrupting the robe folds on the chest and abdomen. Reproduce surviving facial features without smoothing the photographed losses, chips and irregular ear/jaw areas into a perfect generic face. Keep the circular concentric head halo and the enclosing tall pointed FLAME AUREOLE, the distinctive long curling tongues of flame and two damaged small flying-figure remnants high to either side of the halo. Select a few of the real flame paths rather than dense ornamental texture; preserve the irregular lost sections as gaps. The aureole terminates behind the shoulders and lotus seat; no invented freestanding throne or new niche frame. Omit neighboring headless standing attendants because this is an explicitly SELECTED CENTRAL-BUDDHA DETAIL, not a full-cave reconstruction. Retain the complete selected main statue, its halo/flame backplate, surviving flat-topped round lotus seat with worn vertical petal outlines and modest stepped stone platform below as in image3. Simplify the surrounding stone into two or three irregular broken contours, not a large drawn room. Remove modern signs, offerings, bottles, trays, wires, lighting and pipes. Sculpture, broken surfaces, recesses, aureole, and background all stay PURE WHITE with delicate fine BLACK contours, NO black cavities and NO solid shading. Preserve only8to12 subtle actual damage contour interruptions; no scribbled distress, crosshatch, grey pigment, grain or photographic texture. Mainfigure+halo approximately82%of portrait1024x1536 height with all apex and platform inside generous blank margins. Fine restrained line weight and broad empty areas matching image1. No text.

historical_sources.title: 北响堂石窟的新编号及内容简录
historical_sources.publisher: 响堂山石窟研究院 / 响堂山风景区官方网站
historical_sources.evidence: 根据赵立春《文物春秋》2000年第5期编号，大佛洞即北洞、第9窟，时代为东魏、北齐。中心方柱三面开龛、三世佛题材；正面主尊高3.5米，结跏趺坐于圆形莲花座，敷搭双肩式袈裟。

historical_sources.title: North Site | North Cave / 北响堂山 | 北洞
historical_sources.publisher: 芝加哥大学东亚艺术研究中心响堂山石窟项目
historical_sources.evidence: 北洞是最早的大窟。1159年碑记把始凿追记于文宣帝550—559年间，同时期创建题记已不存；中心柱雕三世佛。研究说明造像曾被盗凿，并经历后补，故采用现状图而不臆补残损。

historical_sources.title: Echoes of the Past: The Buddhist Cave Temples of Xiangtangshan
historical_sources.publisher: 史密森学会国立亚洲艺术博物馆
historical_sources.evidence: 博物馆将North Cave（Great Buddha Cave）置于550年代，认为很可能由文宣帝（550—559在位）赞助，但说明窟中缺乏创建题记。为约550年代断代的直接研究依据。

site_recommendation.name: 响堂山石窟
site_recommendation.yearNote: 555仅作约550年代的时间轴中点，不是确切开凿或竣工年。大佛洞整体有东魏、北齐断代范围；主尊图版按博物馆及芝加哥大学研究采用北齐早期约550年代，不把1159年后世碑记当作北齐同时期纪年。
site_recommendation.latlon_note: 采用公开的北响堂窟群定位坐标，供区域地图落点；非第9窟内部主尊的测绘坐标。当前sites.js检索未见峰峰/邯郸地点键，建议新增fengfeng。
site_recommendation.lede: 圆阔的佛面、宽厚的肩背与细密衣纹，被火焰形背光围拢。北响堂大佛洞在鼓山石壁间保存北齐造像的沉静体量，残缺处也留下了漫长的流传痕迹。

facts.label: 北齐早期
facts.text: 大佛洞为北响堂开凿较早的大窟，研究通常置于北齐文宣帝时期、约550年代，确切创建题记已失。

facts.label: 中心柱窟
facts.text: 第9窟采用中心方柱塔庙窟形制，柱上三面雕三世佛；图版取正面主尊，高约3.5米。

facts.label: 残损现状
facts.text: 主尊的双手与部分衣纹已残，圆形头光与火焰背光仍可辨认；窟群雕刻经历风化、盗凿和后世修补。
